locator.panel: loss of C3H7*, product printed first: [C2H5C(CH3)=OH]+ m/z 73, 100%

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s) for this pathway; moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). ARC COUNT, verified by zooming the scan: the single structure carries FOUR arcs in total - one SOLID fishhook that starts at the odd electron drawn as '+.' on the hydroxyl oxygen and ends with a half-arrowhead (barb) on the C-O bond, plus THREE DASHED fishhooks that all end with a barb on that same C-O bond, one starting from each of the three alpha C-C bonds (C-CH3 from above, C-C3H7 and C-C2H5 from below). McLafferty superimposes the three competing alpha cleavages on one drawing; this record takes the two arcs belonging to the C-C3H7 channel (the shared solid oxygen hook = move 1, and the dashed C(1)-C(2) hook = move 2). The third electron of that homolysis - the one that leaves on the propyl radical - is NOT drawn; the book simply writes the alkyl radical loss implicitly by printing only the ion. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the page prints the ionized alcohol as the neutral skeleton with '+.' as one superscript beside OH, so the charge and the odd electron are both placed on oxygen, and the precursor SMILES writes that literally as [OH+:8] with two bonds and one unpaired electron. The reaction is the alpha cleavage that dominates the spectrum: relative rates fall in the order loss of the LARGEST radical first, C3H7* (m/z 73, 100%) > C2H5* (m/z 87, 50%) > CH3* (m/z 101, 10%), which is the point of the equation.

Cross-linked MOD rule variable: IMS_4_17_1 '[C]1([C]2[C]3[C]4)([C]5[C]6)([C]7)([O+.]8)>>[C]5[C]6[C]1([C]7)[O+.]8.[C]2[C]3[C]4'. VERIFIED, not asserted. (i) Left side: the pattern is a tertiary carbinol carbon carrying a 3-carbon chain, a 2-carbon chain, a methyl and an [O+.] - exactly this record's precursor. RDKit substructure test of the equivalent SMARTS [#6]([#6][#6][#6])([#6][#6])([#6])[O+] against the precursor SMILES returns True with a single match that maps the rule's atoms 2-4/5-6/7/8 onto this record's propyl/ethyl/methyl/oxygen, so the reactant side is an exact match and this rule is the m/z 73 channel (it retains C5C6 + C7 on C1 and expels C2C3C4). (ii) Right side is MIS-ENCODED relative to the book, on two counts: the product oxygen is still written [O+.]8 SINGLY bonded to C1, i.e. NO C=O(+) pi bond is formed and the odd electron is left sitting on oxygen, whereas the book's product is the even-electron oxocarbenium [C2H5C(CH3)=OH]+; and the departing alkyl is written [C]2[C]3[C]4 with no radical marker instead of [C.]2. The net effect is that the rule reproduces the correct m/z 73 composition (C4H9O, +1) but as an odd-electron, valence-deficient species (C1 left with three bonds and no radical label) rather than the drawn oxocarbenium. The conservation guardrail in rules/__init__.py does NOT catch this because it only tallies atoms, total charge (+1 -> +1) and total unpaired count (1 -> 1), all of which happen to be numerically unchanged - the error is that the radical sits on the wrong atom. (iii) The unsuffixed sibling IMS_4_17 (line 379) is worse still: its right side is '[C]5[C]6[C]1([C]7)[O+.]8' with the propyl fragment DELETED outright, so it fails atom conservation; it is however never appended to the IMS_chap4_examples export list, so it is dead code and never reaches the DG (grep for IMS_4_17 word-boundary finds only its definition).
